newsitem.title: NEPAL: U.S. couple, three guides feared trapped in Nepal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. couple, three guides feared trapped in Nepal.

text.p: A U.S. couple and their three guides are believed to have been trapped in a snow blizzard in the Himalayan kingdom of Nepal since last week, rescuers said on Thursday after a fourth abortive attempt to find them.

Rescuers said search helicopters looked for Philip Jack Fialkow, 62, a medical school professor from Washington State, and Helen Costas Fialkow, 61, but could not find them in western Nepal's upper Dolpo area.

"Chances of their survival are very rare because they had food only for two days and it is very heavy snow up there," rescue helicopter pilot Kishendra Shahi told Reuters after searching the area on Thursday.
The Fialkow couple were trekking to Tse Gomba, a Buddhist monastery in the upper Dolpo area in far western Nepal.

They trail crosses three mountain passes before reaching the monastery. Search officials said the hikers had only four litres (1.1 U.S. gallon) of kerosene to keep them warm. Their legs were frost bitten and they could not walk, they said.
"The nearest village from the area can be reached only after at least four days walk," Shahi said, adding that the Dolpo area had "very heavy" snowfall this year.
"People in nearby villages said they had not seen such heavy snowfall before," Shahi said.
